title: Make the card work right to left
prompt:
The card is written with physical properties, so it breaks when the wrapper switches to `dir="rtl"`. Without changing the HTML:

- Replace the left border, the left/right padding, the time's right margin, the `text-align` values and the arrow's left margin with **logical** equivalents, so English looks exactly the same.
- In RTL, mirror the arrow icon horizontally (use `:dir(rtl)`).

The checks render the card in both directions.
hints: `text-align: left` becomes `start` and `right` becomes `end`. `padding-inline` takes a start and an end value.
explanation: Logical properties resolve against the element's direction, so `border-inline-start` is the left border in English and the right border in Arabic, and the same goes for `padding-inline`, `margin-inline-end` and `text-align: start/end`. The English rendering is unchanged, and switching `dir` mirrors the card with no extra rules. Directional icons are the exception: a glyph doesn't know which way it should point, so `:dir(rtl)` matches the arrow when its inherited direction is right to left and `scale: -1 1` mirrors it.

checks.ltr-unchanged: In English, the card looks exactly as before
checks.rtl-border: In RTL, the colored border is on the right
checks.rtl-padding: In RTL, the padding follows the text direction
checks.rtl-time-gap: In RTL, the space after the time is on its left
checks.rtl-link-aligned: In RTL, the link aligns to the end and the arrow's gap flips
checks.rtl-arrow-flips: In RTL, the arrow is mirrored
